item.text:
**8B.2 verdict: mixed, with real translation into institutions and budgets, but uneven execution**

I found concrete evidence that Tshisekedi did turn parts of his 2024 program into appointments, budget instruments, and enforcement mechanisms, especially in finance, education, anti-corruption control, and eastern security management. I also found strong counterevidence that execution remained fragmented, patronage-heavy, and partly coercive. I did not find a single standalone 2024 master plan that unified all these moves; the record is pieced together from appointments, IMF/World Bank program documents, and official crisis readouts.

**Accepted claims**

- **Government formation turned the post-election program into a concrete cabinet.**  
  **Reuters** | **2024-05-29** | https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/DR-Congo-names-new-government-after-months-of-delay-46846207/  
  Tshisekedi ended months of cabinet delay by naming Judith Suminwa prime minister, Vital Kamerhe as speaker, and then appointing a 54-minister cabinet that included a defense minister, finance minister, and mines minister. This is direct evidence of translating political priorities into staffing and portfolio choices, even if the long delay shows coalition bargaining and patronage pressures.  
  **QIDs:** 8B.2, 8B.1

- **The presidency framed Suminwa’s appointment as a technocratic, gender-signaling choice.**  
  **Ministère de la Communication et Médias** | **2024-04-01** | https://communication.gouv.cd/actualites/communications-du-gouvernement/18/madame-judith-suminwa-tuluka-nommee-premiere-ministre-de-la-republique-democratique-du-congo  
  The presidency said Suminwa was chosen for her skills and development-planning experience, and presented her as the first woman to become prime minister. This is concrete evidence of a stated governing preference for competence and inclusion rather than only loyalty.  
  **QIDs:** 8B.2, 8B.1

- **A key fiscal portfolio was given to a career technocrat.**  
  **ACP** | **2024-05-30** | https://acp.cd/economie/rdc-fwamba-likunde-un-technocrate-rompu-a-la-tete-du-ministere-des-finances-par-elysee-kakese/  
  ACP described Doudou Fwamba as an experienced finance technocrat with public-finance expertise. That is direct evidence that Tshisekedi backed the program with a professional appointment in a strategic budget ministry, not just a political loyalist.  
  **QIDs:** 8B.2, 8B.1

- **The IMF program spelled out concrete fiscal controls, timelines, and institutional reforms.**  
  **IMF** | **2024-11-13** | https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/11/13/pr-24416-drc-imf-reaches-agreement-on-ecf-and-rsf  
  The IMF-backed program tied Tshisekedi’s agenda to specific mechanisms: stronger public-expenditure-chain controls, operationalization of the Treasury and Treasury Single Account, gradual decentralization of spending authorization to line ministries, stricter revenue mobilization, and governance/transparency reforms. This is the clearest evidence of a translated governing program with implementation machinery.  
  **QIDs:** 8B.2, 8B.1

- **The 2024 IMF staff report showed the government beginning to operationalize those fiscal mechanisms.**  
  **IMF** | **2024-07-03** | https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/07/03/pr24253-drc-imf-exec-board-concludes-2024-art-iv-consult-completes-6th-rev-ecf-arr  
  The IMF said the authorities were cleaning up the civil-service payroll using biometric identification, reorganizing civil-service social security, and working on Treasury Single Account and expenditure-chain reforms. That is concrete evidence of policy translated into administrative instruments, though the report also says progress was slow.  
  **QIDs:** 8B.2

- **Education policy was translated into a project with budgets, recruitment rules, and planning tools.**  
  **World Bank** | **2024-02-28** | https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/02/28/democratic-republic-of-congo-afe-expanding-and-equipping-primary-school-classrooms-for-better-learning-outcomes  
  The PEQIP project funded classrooms, materials, teacher training, merit-based recruitment, more qualified female teachers, stronger information systems, and decentralized strategic planning. This is a clear example of a policy direction being turned into an implementable sector program with operational design.  
  **QIDs:** 8B.2, 8B.1

- **Security policy was translated into formal command structures and orders.**  
  **Présidence RDC** | **2024-07-05** | https://presidence.cd/actualite-detail/actualite/securite_a_lest_le_chef_de_letat_a_reuni_la_task_force_du_haut_commandement_militaire  
  Tshisekedi convened the high-command task force, received tactical assessments, and ordered the military to launch actions to safeguard territorial integrity. This is direct evidence of concrete enforcement and command coordination, not just rhetoric.  
  **QIDs:** 8B.2, 8B.1

- **Disarmament and stabilization were framed as a national institutional program, not an ad hoc slogan.**  
  **ACP** | **2024-03-22** | https://acp.cd/nation/programme-de-desarmement-et-demobilisation-une-alternative-pour-la-paix-et-la-cohesion-sociale/  
  ACP reported that P-DDRCS was presented as a national stabilization, peace, and cohesion program meant to restore state authority where absent. This is strong evidence of a named institutional mechanism for conflict management and armed-group control.  
  **QIDs:** 8B.2, 8B.1

- **The Court of Accounts was publicly strengthened as a control institution.**  
  **Présidence RDC** | **2024-10-07** | https://www.presidence.cd/actualite-detail/actualite/le_chef_de_l_etat_a_assiste_a_louverture_de_la_session_extraordinaire_du_conseil_superieur_de_la_cour_des_comptes  
  The presidency backed the Court of Accounts’ control function, and the court explicitly linked Tshisekedi’s support to anti-corruption oversight and public-finance control. That is direct evidence of an enforcement-and-oversight mechanism being activated inside the state.  
  **QIDs:** 8B.2, 8B.1

**Counterevidence**

- **The cabinet process was delayed by internal jostling, which weakens the clean “program to execution” story.**  
  **Reuters** | **2024-05-29** | https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/DR-Congo-names-new-government-after-months-of-delay-46846207/  
  Reuters said internal bargaining delayed the cabinet for months and the final government was larger than expected despite pressure to cut costs. This suggests patronage and coalition management still shaped implementation more than a disciplined policy pipeline.  
  **QIDs:** 8B.2, 8B.1

- **Security implementation was still weakly controlled and heavily proxy-based.**  
  **Reuters** | **2024-07-17** | https://theprint.in/world/army-disarray-hobbles-congos-fight-with-rwanda-backed-rebels-officers-say/2160048/  
  Officers described mismanagement, poor logistics, demoralized troops, and reliance on uncontrolled Wazalendo militias. Tshisekedi reportedly told them to be brought in line, but the broader picture is a fragmented enforcement apparatus, not a fully translated program.  
  **QIDs:** 8B.2, 8B.1

- **The constitutional review push pointed toward regime entrenchment rather than programmatic governance.**  
  **Reuters** | **2024-10-24** | https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/congo-president-tshisekedi-draws-criticism-over-constitutional-reform-plans-2024-10-24/  
  Reuters reported a commission to explore constitutional revisions that could remove term limits and enable a third term. This is evidence of a concrete political-control project, but it cuts against a clean reading of institutionalized public-program implementation.  
  **QIDs:** 8B.2, 8B.1

- **Public-resource management around elections remained opaque.**  
  **Reuters** | **2024-01-15** | https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/congo-election-commission-overspent-awarded-opaque-contracts-report-2024-01-15/  
  Reuters cited a civil-society report saying CENI could not account for about $400 million and used opaque procurement. That is negative evidence for disciplined budgeting and transparent administrative enforcement.  
  **QIDs:** 8B.2

**Search gap**

I did not find a single 2024 master policy document from Tshisekedi that clearly unified all priorities, budgets, and enforcement tools in one place. The best evidence comes from separate but converging sources: cabinet appointments, IMF program documents, World Bank project design, official security readouts, and the Court of Accounts.
